# IR testdata

`counters-10-5.json` and `counters-10-6.json` are the IR encoding of the
Spike's synthetic throughput model (`engine/internal/spike/counters.go`,
Promela in `internal/spike/testdata/counters.pml`): N processes, each with a
local byte counter incremented modulo K; the reachable graph is exactly K^N
states (100 000 and 1 000 000), every state has N enabled transitions, and
there is no deadlock. They are generated, not hand-written:

    MCD_GEN_TESTDATA=1 go test ./explore -run TestGenerateTestdata

The 1e5 model is used by `features/g0-engine.feature` for the budget
scenarios; both are used by the throughput measurement in
`steps/g0-confirmation.md` (K1 condition: interpreted IR within 20x of the
Spike's compiled-in models).

`por-visible.json` is the model of `features/g7-por.feature`'s visibility
scenario (partial-order reduction, `mcd check --por`): process A writes the
global `x` twice while B and C each count a private byte to 3; the invariant
`x != 2` is violated and the reach property `x == 1` holds. It is generated by
the same command from `porVisible()` in `explore/models_test.go`.

`weakfair-claim-last.json`, `weakfair-claim-first.json` and
`weakfair-claim-middle.json` are one model with its three processes in three
orders: P0 flips a bit for ever, P1 is blocked for ever (`0 == 1`), and a never
claim accepts everything. The claim is the last process in the first file, the
first in the second and the middle one in the third. The Promela frontend, the
LTL claim and `np_` always put the claim last; an IR from `--ir` or from an
inline `ir` argument of `mc_check` need not. `features/g4-ltl.feature` and
`explore/weakfair_test.go` hold the verdicts: `violated` under every fairness
setting in every order.

`nrpr-property.json` is hand-written (no frontend produces it): two processes
that each set the global `x`, no read of `_nr_pr` and no process that leaves the
live-process table, and two properties that read `_nr_pr` through the IR op
`nrpr` (`none`: reach `_nr_pr == 0`, `two`: invariant `_nr_pr == 2`), next to
one that does not (`sane`). It is the command-line counterpart of the MCP
scenarios of `features/g5-ctl-v1.feature` that send such properties to a model
whose processes keep no table: the properties are `not-executed`, the others
are answered (`steps/fix-nrpr-confirmation.md`).

`por-dormant.json` is the model of `features/g7-por.feature`'s scenario on the
refusal of a dynamic process that goes back to its dormant location without
leaving the process table (performance plan, step 6): process `S` runs `D`,
and `D`'s last edge returns to the dormant location with no `leave`. The Promela
frontend never emits that shape. It is generated by the same command from
`porDormantReentry()` in `explore/por_run_test.go`.

`par-initial.json`, `par-initial-error.json`, `par-decided.json`,
`par-skip-reach.json`, `par-skip-inv.json`,
`par-assert-overflow.json`, `par-atomic-loop.json`, `par-claim.json`, `par-fanout.json` and
`par-fanout-assert.json` are the
directed models of `features/g8-parallel.feature` (parallel exploration: the
checks of the initial state, an evaluation error in the expression of a decided
property, the same error on a state that another property is decided on (the
two `par-skip-*` models: the other checks of that state must still be made), an
error of a step that also fails its assert, an atomic loop that
never blocks, a never claim that the run does not ask for, and a model whose
states have 600 successors each, with and without an assert that every
transition fails). They are generated by

    MCD_GEN_TESTDATA=1 go test ./explore -run TestGenerateParallelTestdata

from `parInitialViolation()`, `parInitialError()`, `parDecided()`,
`parSkippedReach()`, `parSkippedInvariant()`, `parAssertOverflow()`, `parAtomicLoop()`, `parClaimModelIR()` and `fanOutModel()` in
`explore/parallel_models_test.go`.
